extracted.intended_audience: cartoonists and caricaturists (professionals, amateurs, youth) submitting work to national and international cartoon competitions
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and evaluation criteria for entering and judging cartoons/caricatures in international and national competitions (eligibility, file/physical format, originality, jury process, rights and prizes). Applies to artists preparing submissions and contest organizers setting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theme adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: Works must address the announced theme when a theme is specified (e.g., "Earthquake", "Freedom", "The Hat", "The madness of war").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winning works will be those that best capture, analyze, contrast, promote and disseminate the theme, or otherwise interpret it as the contest requires. Some contests allow open theme (participants free to choose).

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and unpublished status
rubrics_metrics.description: Works must be completely original and unpublished; adaptations of others' originals or works that have received prizes in other competitions are typically not accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several calls explicitly disqualify similar, imitation or stolen cartoons and note that the sender remains responsible for originality; organizers may cancel prizes if plagiarism is found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of entries per participant
rubrics_metrics.description: Contests set limits on how many works each author may submit (common limits: up to 3, 4 or 5; some allow unlimited entries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules vary by competition: e.g., up to 3 works per section; maximum 5 entries per person in some contests; some competitions allow unlimited entries (state explicitly when unlimited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Age categories and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Competitions frequently have separate categories (adults / youth / children) with age requirements or minimum ages (e.g., participants over 16, or adults 18+).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some contests require entrants to indicate age and place works in the appropriate category; children’s winners are listed separately in some events.

rubrics_metrics.name: File/physical format, size and resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Digital submissions must meet specified image dimensions, dpi and file types (e.g., A3/A4, 300 dpi, specific pixel minima, max file sizes, allowed formats like JPG, JPEG, TIFF, EPS, PSD, PDF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from page: min. 2480 x 3500 pixels (A4 300dpi), A3 (297x420mm) max, 5 MB per picture, JPEG/TIFF; digital drawings: 300 dpi, max 3MB. Follow the exact contest technical specs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique and color restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: The technique is usually free (any technique allowed), but some contests restrict color: e.g., only black & white allowed (gray tones not accepted) or permit black & white or colour; moving images are disallowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One contest explained reasons for black & white only (preserve line and quips; avoid AI/illustration substitutes). Others explicitly allow all graphic and photographic techniques and digital drawing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text/language rules within cartoons
rubrics_metrics.description: Some contests forbid text in the image ("works should not contain text" / "must not contain text"); others allow text but require it be in a specific language (e.g., Spanish) or label translations for entries from outside a country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If words are allowed, some calls require they be in the contest language (e.g., Spanish) or that entries containing text be labeled; follow each call’s language instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature, pseudonym and anonymity procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Many contests require works to be signed with a pseudonym or to be submitted anonymously with identity provided separately (e.g., pseudonym on the work and a separate file with real name and details).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical instruction: sign with a pseudonym; send a separate file listing pseudonym, real name, address, occupation, telephone, email and short bio. Some require name/address written on the back of physical works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method, labeling and metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific submission channels (email address, online form, postal address) and required metadata (subject line, file naming, artist name, title, contact details) are mandated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: send to a specified email with subject “For the competition”; include artist name, surname, first name, title and email; on the back of physical cartoons state title, surname, first name and address. Participation valid only with completed form where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion for works previously awarded or exhibited
rubrics_metrics.description: Many contests exclude works that have been awarded in other competitions or previously exhibited in specific jurisdictions (e.g., not exhibited in Belgium).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some competitions explicitly state that previously awarded works are not accepted; others allow previously published/exhibited works—read each call carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism/similarity checks and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizers will check for plagiarism or similarity; if a winning work is found similar to a previously published piece, prizes may be cancelled and redistributed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contests may submit suspect works for objection and cancel plagiarized works before final results; jury can withdraw prizes after deliberation if plagiarism is discovered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jury composition, selection process and finality of decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: A professional/international jury of cartoonists or representatives judges submissions; their decisions are final and they may declare prizes void or reallocate them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some calls describe jury stages (selection for exhibition then prize selection), secrecy of jury composition until decisions are published, and reserve the right to not award prizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jury evaluation criteria (artistic value, topicality, content)
rubrics_metrics.description: At least one contest specifies judging on "artistic value, topicality and content (the theme)" when selecting and awarding works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where explicit, the jury will assess artistic merit, relevance to theme and message/content; other contests imply quality-based judgment without listing explicit metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership, publication and reproduction rights
rubrics_metrics.description: By participating, entrants often grant the organizing body rights to use their entries for advertising, catalogs, exhibitions and promotion; some state submitted works become property of the organizers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical clauses: organizers may use the works for exhibition, video recordings, distribution, books, brochures, catalogs and city advertisements. Some require additional permission for other uses; in some contests submitted works become the organizer's property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return, storage and disposal of submitted works
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizers specify whether originals will be returned, storage duration and return conditions (e.g., return at entrant's expense, stored for up to 2 years, or originals not returned and added to a documentation centre).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: originals sent by mail will be accepted; originals will only be sent back on written request at sender's cost; selected works remain at organizers’ disposal until a specified date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to provide originals for awarded works
rubrics_metrics.description: Winners may be required to send original versions of artworks before receiving prizes or for exhibition purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several contests state the original of award-winning works must be sent to the festival secretariat to receive the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent to contest rules and organizer rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Participation implies acceptance of the rules; organizers reserve the right to make changes and to resolve unspecified situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical language: participation presupposes acceptance of rules; the jury/organizers are empowered to resolve any situation not specified and to introduce necessary modifications for smooth running.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy and use of personal information
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal information (name, email, address) will be used to inform participants about the competition and to notify winners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some contests explicitly state consent to use personal data for competition communication and promotional purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prize terms, collection and tax compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Prizes are awarded per contest rules with amounts and may be subject to tax requirements; unclaimed prizes may be reallocated after a specified time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: cash prizes with amounts listed; prizes may be collected upon compliance with tax requirements of Mexico and contestant's country; unclaimed prizes within three months may be used by the organizer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical presentation constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical works must meet packaging and presentation rules (e.g., packaged flat, not folded; no works under glass or framed; A4/A3 sizes required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some calls prohibit framed works or glass, require sturdy paper of A4 size for post submissions, and specify how to mark the reverse side.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital submission technicalities (naming, max size, allowed file types)
rubrics_metrics.description: Digital submissions must conform to technical rules like minimum pixel dimensions, DPI, maximum megabyte size and permitted file formats (jpg, jpeg, eps, tif, psd, pdf, tiff).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contests give concrete specs (e.g., min. 2480 x 3500 px, DPI 300; allowed file types: jpg jpeg eps tif psd pdf); failure to meet specs may invalidate participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language requirements for accompanying materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Biographies, autobiographies or labels sometimes must be provided in a specific language (e.g., English only) or entries with text must be labeled when not in the local language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: author must send a short autobiography in English only; outside entries containing text must be labeled; some accept any official languages plus English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category-specific documentation and proof
rubrics_metrics.description: For category entry (e.g., professionals, amateurs, university), required documentation must be provided (e.g., short biography, proof of regular publication, university affiliation certificate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Professional category may require a link proving regular publication; Spanish university category requires certificate of affiliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on content types (no moving images)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contests commonly prohibit moving images or animations; cartoons must be single images or short comic strips (static).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly: no moving images allowed; cartoons may consist of a single image or a short comic strip.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection announcement and timeline requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Contests provide deadlines, selection announcement dates and jury meeting dates; participants must meet submission windows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: submission windows (e.g., Jan 1–Aug 15), deadlines (e.g., Jan 31, Nov 17), jury meeting dates and publication dates for results; participation not valid if late or incomplete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibition and catalog inclusion obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Selected and prize-winning works will be included in exhibitions and printed/electronic catalogs; participants typically authorize such inclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizers may publish winners in catalogs, websites, and promotional materials; selected participants may receive a catalog copy (possibly at their expense).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of organizers to use works for promotion and education
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizers reserve the right to further use competition works for exhibitions, information purposes and to popularize the genre; this use can include promotional printed works and itinerant exhibitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants often grant rights for organizer's promotional use (catalogues, posters, calendars, social media), sometimes without additional remuneration beyond credit to the artist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance and disqualification clause
rubrics_metrics.description: Any work not complying with contest rules will be disqualified; the jury can declare a prize void if they consider no submission of sufficient quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation presupposes acceptance of these rules and non-compliant works will not be published or awarded; jury decisions are final.
